Class InvitationService

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.emaillink.InvitationService
public class InvitationService extends Object
Invites a person by email address: creates an identity for them, signs it in with that address, gives it roles, and sends it a sign-in link in an InvitationMessage. Accepting the invitation is signing in. Behind POST /who/invitations, and usable from application code as it is.

The order is guaranteed:

  1. In one transaction: the identity is created, the address registered to it, each role assigned, and IdentityInvited published synchronously, so a listener can write the application's own data in the same transaction. If any step throws, a listener included, the whole transaction rolls back: no identity, address or role remains, and no link is sent. who's own events from these steps, such as IdentityCreated, are delivered only if it commits.
  2. Only after that transaction has committed, the sign-in link is issued by EmailLinkIssuer.issue(String, String) with no transaction open, so a link is only ever sent for an identity that exists, and no database connection is held while the email goes out. The invitation stands whatever becomes of the link: Invitation.linkOutcome says, and a link that is not sent is logged at WARN without the address or the token.

This service applies no policy about who may grant which roles: it is for trusted application code. who-admin's endpoint applies its own.

  • Method Details

    • invite

      public Invitation invite(@Nullable String email, Set<String> roleNames)
      Invites the address with the named roles, in the order the class describes. Call it outside any transaction: the link is issued after the invitation commits, with no transaction open, which a caller's transaction would postpone.
      Parameters:
      email - the address, as typed; registered normalized
      roleNames - the names of the roles to give the identity; empty for none
      Returns:
      the new identity and what became of its sign-in link
      Throws:
      InvalidInvitationException - before anything is created, if the address is missing or is not an address, a role name is blank, or roles are asked for without who-rbac; and, with everything rolled back, if a name names no role
      EmailAddressTakenException - if the address already belongs to an identity, or a concurrent invitation or registration of it wins; nothing is created
      IllegalStateException - if called inside a transaction
